episodes.205712: During the afternoon and early evening hours of September 16th, isolated thunderstorms developed around the KC metro. These storms brought damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.205738: Monsoon moisture returned to southern, eastern, and much of central New Mexico on September 16th. This higher moisture combined with disturbances rotating around the southern periphery of an upper low over the northern and central Rocky Mountains resulted in the development of showers and thunderstorms during the midday hours across these portions of the state. A thunderstorm produced a wet microburst over the Las Vegas Municipal Airport during the mid-afternoon hours resulting in an 81 mph wind gust at the site. Additionally, slow moving thunderstorms on I-25 at Algodones produced flash flooding on the highway and railroad, resulting in backups and delays for several hours during the evening. Showers and thunderstorms across the region tapered off during the late evening hours after sunset. ||An upper level disturbance over Colorado combined with a backdoor front draped across far northeast New Mexico resulted in the development of severe thunderstorms across northern Colfax and northeastern Union Counties from the mid-afternoon to mid-evening hours. Large hail up to golf ball size was observed near Sugarite Canyon State Park and in Clayton. Thunderstorms across far northeast New Mexico tapered off during the late evening hours as the backdoor front surged south through eastern New Mexico.
episodes.205790: Isolated thunderstorms moved through Middle Tennessee during the afternoon of September 16, 2025. In Hermitage, strong winds from these thunderstorms were observed as they snapped a few branches and one tree.
episodes.206302: Typical summertime pulse thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of September 14-17. While most storms remained below severe limits, a few storms did produce localized damaging downburst winds and large hail.
episodes.206303: Typical summertime pulse thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of September 16. While most storms remained below severe limits, a few storms did produce large hail in Cherokee County, Kansas.
episodes.206518: During the late afternoon and evening hours on September 16th, a couple of pop up thunderstorms developed across much of Iowa and produced sporadic instances of large hail. In Floyd County, two particular storm cells rapidly developed and dropped hail between quarter to golf ball size in portions of the county.
episodes.206589: Two lines of strong thunderstorms developed over southeast Wyoming in the morning of September 16th, with another line developing and strengthening during the middle of the afternoon. These storms moved east and briefly became severe and produced winds gusts over 58 mph.
episodes.206590: Two lines of strong thunderstorms developed over southeast Wyoming in the morning of September 16th, with another line developing and strengthening during the middle of the afternoon. These storms moved east and briefly became severe and produced winds gusts over 58 mph.
episodes.206683: A very strong thunderstorm developed near McCook during the afternoon, remaining nearly stationary for roughly two hours over the town before moving east.  During this time the thunderstorm produced hail over three inches in diameter, wind gusts up to 60 MPH, and closed to six inches of rainfall.  The prolonged heavy rainfall caused rushing water to be close to a foot deep in the low lying areas of McCook.||Elsewhere thunderstorm activity produced much smaller hail in Hitchcock and Dundy counties.
episodes.206684: Scattered thunderstorms developed over Northwest Kansas in the late afternoon and early evening.  A thunderstorm moving over Atwood had the largest hail reported; golf ball size.  Elsewhere wind gusts around 60 MPH were measured at St. Francis and Oberlin.  A dust storm associated with thunderstorm winds was reported north of Blakeman along a broken line of thunderstorms as the storms moved north.
episodes.206791: A weak shortwave trough traversed southeast across Southern Arkansas and Northcentral Louisiana during the afternoon of September 16th, as temperatures climbed into the mid and upper 90s. As a result, moderate to strong instability developed given the existing low level moisture in place, with increased large scale ascent contributing to the development of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of Southern Arkansas and Northcentral Louisiana during the late afternoon and early evening hours. These storms produced instances of damaging winds which downed trees and power lines, as well as isolated instances of large hail across portions of Ouachita, Union, and Lincoln Parishes before diminishing during the evening.
episodes.206797: A weak shortwave trough traversed southeast across Southern Arkansas and Northcentral Louisiana during the afternoon of September 16th, as temperatures climbed into the mid and upper 90s. As a result, moderate to strong instability developed given the existing low level moisture in place, with increased large scale ascent contributing to the development of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of Southern Arkansas and Northcentral Louisiana during the late afternoon and early evening hours. These storms produced instances of damaging winds which downed several trees across Columbia County Arkansas before diminishing during the evening.
episodes.206809: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon and early evening of the 16th. Moderate instability developed during the afternoon in the hot and humid air mass, but wind fields and wind shear were very weak. This combination of instability and wind shear resulted in intense, but short-lived thunderstorms, the strongest of which produced hail up to quarter size.
episodes.207261: A few thunderstorms developed ahead of a weak cold front across northeastern Minnesota during the early evening hours of the 16th. One storm produced hail to the size of ping pong balls in Babbitt, but no additional reports were received as the storms remained over rural areas.
episodes.207300: During the afternoon hours of Sept 16th, storms brought large hail and damaging wind gusts to portions of Johnson County, KS.
episodes.207320: Thunderstorm activity across East Central Colorado produced hail up to quarter size near Vernon and a tornado south of Burlington.  The landspout formed along a nearly stationary boundary that extended from north to south.
episodes.207522: Funnel clouds developed in Ward County near Minot in the afternoon hours as a low pressure system moved through northern North Dakota. Later in the evening thunderstorms moved into southwest North Dakota ahead of a short-wave trough ejecting ahead of an upper level low pressure system over southern Montana. One storm became severe producing 60 mph wind gusts northeast of Bucyrus in Adams County.
episodes.207530: An upper-level disturbance moving through weak northwest flow over the Mid-South kicked off isolated showers and thunderstorms across north Mississippi during the evening hours of September 15, 2025. Enough instability was present to help a couple of storms intensify to severe limits and produce damaging winds.
episodes.207582: Thunderstorms developed around midday, along a frontal boundary, in the northeastern Nebraska Panhandle. As this broken line of storms tracked east into the Sandhills, southwestern and north central Nebraska, wind gusts up to 63 MPH and hail up to ping pong ball size was reported.
episodes.207652: Diurnal heating allowed strong afternoon storms to develop across southwest Louisiana.
episodes.207662: An area of low pressure developed along remnant frontal boundaries offshore of the North Carolina coast September 14 into September 15. This system slowly meandered northward in the early hours of September 16, before turning northwest and making landfall near the mouth of the Chesapeake Bay in the late afternoon. As the low approached the Virginia coast, it deepened and developed a circular area of heavy rain around the center of circulation. Widespread heavy rainfall and locally strong wind gusts occurred in coastal portions of southeast Virginia, persisting into the evening hours of September 16.
episodes.207732: An area of low pressure tracked to the north of the region during the day on the 16th, with an associated front draped across northeast Utah and northwest Colorado. An upper level jet streak was tracking across region during this period as well, providing some extra lift. Instability in the realm of 600-800 J/kg of CAPE was also present across this region, as well as ample moisture. All these combined to fire off strong to severe thunderstorms across northeast Utah and northwest Colorado during the afternoon hours. While this set up was not as potent as that seen during the 11th to the 13th, it was enough to cause some flash flooding and severe thunderstorm winds.
episodes.207741: A landspout tornado was spotted near Sahuarita, AZ. The tornado caused no damage or injury. The time and location of the tornado was estimated by radar. The landspout tornado was left unrated due to the remote location and would be difficult to survey.
episodes.207756: An area of low pressure brought gusty winds and heavy rainfall to southeast Virginia and the Virginia Eastern Shore on September 16. Multiple bands of heavy rainfall rotated inland as the low approached the coast from the late morning into the evening hours, with widespread reports of flooding throughout the region during the day. Higher-than-normal high tide cycles also exacerbated impacts from freshwater flooding. Peak storm total rainfall amounts were in the 4-9 range across southside Hampton Roads, including 7.72 at the Oceana Naval Air Station (KNTU) AWOS.
episodes.207782: A retreating surface boundary south of the area, ample available moisture, and diurnal heating permitted a strong thunderstorm to develop in southern Broward County on the 16th of September.
episodes.207822: An area of low pressure tracked to the north of the region during the day on the 16th, with an associated front draped across northeast Utah and northwest Colorado. An upper level jet streak was tracking across region during this period as well, providing some extra lift. Instability in the realm of 600-800 J/kg of CAPE was also present across this region, as well as ample moisture. All these combined to fire off strong to severe thunderstorms across northeast Utah and northwest Colorado during the afternoon hours. A few storms in northeast Utah produced some hail.
episodes.207845: A strong/severe thunderstorm produce wind gusts up to 58 mph and one inch hail over eastern Adams, eastern Arapahoe, and western Washington Counties.
episodes.207964: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed over northeast Louisiana and produced hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.207965: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed over Mississippi on September 16th and 17th and produced hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.208321: An omega block pattern set up in mid September and on the 16th Iowa was just west of the ridge axis. This resulted in a hot and humid period and MLCAPE was around 2000-3000 J/kg. The 0-6 km shear was weak under the ridge at under 20 kts. In the deeply unstable environment, pulse thunderstorms were able to develop quickly but the lack of shear prevented better organization and the storms would eventually collapse on themselves. This resulted in widespread scattered thunderstorms across Iowa that produced quarter sized hail and then collapsed and produced wind gusts of 50-60 mph. The lack of flow also meant that storm motions were around 5-10 mph. In an environment with precipitable water over 1.5 inches and deep warm cloud layers allowing for efficient rain production, the slow storm motions resulted in areas with 4-6 inches of rain. Even so, dry antecedent conditions prevent widespread hydrologic problems. Flash flooding was reported in Fort Dodge when thunderstorm set up over the town, resulting in closed roads and stalled vehicles across town. Storms diminished in strength overnight but remained efficient rain producers into the early morning of September 17th.
episodes.208343: A few isolated thunderstorms that remained nearly stationary over the Black Hills mainly impacted Custer and Meade counties. The strongest storms ended up producing low end severe weather with large hail occurring in Custer county.
